main_body: Japanese-style townhouse: dark blue-grey tiled roof with a ridge, a cream plaster band with slit windows, a small lower eave roof, and a brown wooden lattice facade with a central dark doorway
top_band: Pale blue-grey ridge cap at rows 0-5, then a large tile roof slope (rows 6-30) in mid and dark blue-grey with lighter tile highlights. The slope ends at a lighter lip (rows 28-29) and a dark eave line (rows 30-31).
evidence: Down the middle column: ridge cap, then a tall tile roof slope that reads as a surface seen from above, then a light lip and a dark eave shadow at rows 30-31. Below that are the plaster wall (rows 32-40), a second small eave roof (rows 41-47) and the lattice facade with the dark doorway set back inside its frame (rows 48-78). The roof slopes are clearly visible and there is a real front face, so this is 3/4. The roof tile columns are stylised but still read as a slope, not a flat band.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 blue-grey steps with per-tile highlights, and the wood lattice and straw carry several tones. The outlines lean blue on the roof and brown on the wood, so they are not pure black. Against the references, the cream plaster band is large, nearly flat areas with only a few shade columns, with no speckle or grain. The dark doorway interior is also a flat fill. The roof tile pattern is a regular vertical stripe, without the scalloped per-tile shading of the Beodeul roofs. Overall it is somewhat thinner and flatter than the references.
